newsitem.title: USA: Colonial will continue Line 2 rationing in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Colonial will continue Line 2 rationing in Feb.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline Co said Wednesday that it would continue rationing through February on Line 2, the distillate line with capacity to run 960,000 barrels per day from Houston to the northeast U.S.
Line 2 is the main pipeline feeding distillates -- heating oil and diesel -- to the northeast market.

"Based on the continued strength of Line 2 nominations for cyles four and six (most of February)...the allocation (rationing) of Line 2 will continue" through to the end of February, Colonial said in a statement.
Line 2, which carries distillates from Houston to Greensboro, North Carolina, where it splits into Lines 3 and 4, has been under allocation since December.

Demand for heating oil, or high sulphur distillate, in the Northeast led to the surge in nominations, with inventories there remaining at very low historical levels. The Northeast is the world's largest heating oil market.
The arterial Colonial Pipeline extends from Houston to Linden, New Jersey, on the edge of New York Harbor and also includes a 1.2 million bpd gasoline line.

Ten companies make up the Atlanta-based Colonial consortium including Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Union Oil, a unit of Unocal Corp, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
